mcp.anti_evasion.chip: Closing check submitted ({severity}){counts} — content saved into the closing report
mcp.anti_evasion.g_required: g is required: version-control closing (what is committed, what is not and why; write "none" if nothing changed)
mcp.anti_evasion.hint_ai_decided: Things the user did not ask for and the AI decided itself; give [] if none
mcp.anti_evasion.hint_goal: What the user asked for this time, one item each (at least one)
mcp.anti_evasion.hint_principles: Tradeoffs touching the user's long-term principles/direction; give [] if none
mcp.anti_evasion.kind_invalid: ai_decided item {index}: kind must be one of {kinds}
mcp.anti_evasion_report.description: Closing self-check report; its content is saved as a closing report for the user to read, and chat keeps only a one-line receipt. Required by the Stop gate when core files were changed and completion is declared. The reader is a user who did not watch the work: write the body in plain language with no internal jargon (if unavoidable, add a plain-language gloss), and put file:line / commit / path / rule codes in each item's tech or in a / g. The core is three categories, written separately and all required: goal = what the user asked for this time (one item per request, each tied to the user's own words; say what was done, how it was confirmed, what was not done and why); principles = how you traded off wherever the user's long-term principles, design yardsticks or system direction were touched; ai_decided = what the user did not ask for and you decided yourself (tradeoffs, out-of-scope changes, assumptions relied on without verification, environment changes). The report lays the three categories side by side by volume: if the user's requests get one line and your own decisions get a long list, the user sees it at a glance - put effort and length into what the user asked for. The remaining fields are the system ledger (a, b, d, g, h, i, j_evidence_path, k_followups are required; fill "none" when nothing happened, (k) does not accept an empty string). Submit everything at once at closing: put knowledge to record in harvest_items (same as the items of knowledge_harvest_report), no separate call to that tool is needed. Order: first finish writing the knowledge worth keeping with atom_write, then call this tool - the report is a closing check, not a to-do list; (d) "not yet written / see next action" or (h) "next action = write an atom" is bounced by the Stop gate and you must write it and resubmit. This tool only returns a chip and writes no state (one-writer: state/persistence belongs exclusively to the Python PostToolUse).
mcp.anti_evasion_report.param_a: Technical appendix: what was changed where (`- file:line — what changed`); it goes into the appendix; "none" if nothing. Required
mcp.anti_evasion_report.param_ai_decided: Required, give [] if none: what the user did not ask for and you decided yourself, one item each - anything the user would not know about without watching the work counts.

tradeoff = you picked an approach or skipped a step; out_of_scope = you touched something outside the request; assumption = an assumption relied on while working but not verified; side_effect = environment changes (installing packages, changing settings, restarting services, creating schedules, background processes still running)
Optional: technical details; kept in a collapsed section
What was done / assumed, in plain language
Why it was decided this way; whether the user should look back at it
mcp.anti_evasion_report.param_b: AI evasion report (ignored / hidden phenomena); fill only if it happened, otherwise "none"
mcp.anti_evasion_report.param_d: Memory-capture ledger: before filling, scan five sources - (1) the user's corrections / rejections / restatements (-> feedback) (2) mechanisms or pitfalls that took >=2 retries or a lookup to understand (3) facts found externally (with date) (4) tradeoffs / contracts / preferences I made (5) existing atoms proven wrong or needing additions. For each item write `- <item> → written to atom <name>` (the atom_write is already done) or `- <item> → not written (one-sentence reason)`; a decision not to write must also leave a trace. ⛔ "not yet written / to be added / see next action" is not accepted - that pushes memory to the next turn, and is rejected and blocks Stop; if worth writing, write it before calling this tool. If a harvest report (knowledge_harvest_report) was already submitted this turn, you may fill only "see harvest report". "none" if nothing. Required
mcp.anti_evasion_report.param_g: Technical appendix, version-control closing: which changes are committed (one sentence with hash), which are not and why (concurrent session progress / awaiting decision / privacy); not committing was your own decision, so list it as another ai_decided item. "none" if nothing changed. Required
mcp.anti_evasion_report.param_goal: Required, at least one item: what the user asked for this time, one item per request. Split into as many items as the user asked for things; a request you did not do must still be listed (write "not done" in done).
mcp.anti_evasion_report.param_goal_done: What was done, in plain language a reader who did not watch the work can follow
mcp.anti_evasion_report.param_goal_not_d: The part of this item that was not done, with the reason; write "none" if it was all done
mcp.anti_evasion_report.param_goal_said: The user's own words, copied verbatim for that segment (a sub-agent copies the user's words quoted in its dispatch; if the dispatch quotes none, copy the dispatch sentence and mark it "dispatch:")
mcp.anti_evasion_report.param_goal_tech: Optional: technical details (file:line, commit, commands); kept in a collapsed section
mcp.anti_evasion_report.param_goal_verif: How you confirmed it was done right, in plain language with numbers (what was run, how many passed); if not verified write "not verified: reason"
mcp.anti_evasion_report.param_h: Closing verdict: a single sentence - "can close" or "next action = ...". List as next action only what the user must do (restart to verify, make a decision); writing atoms / adding tests / committing are things you can do yourself, so finish them before submitting. Required
mcp.anti_evasion_report.param_harvest_it: Knowledge-harvest list (optional, same format as the items of knowledge_harvest_report; once submitted no separate call to that tool is needed, and (d) may say "see harvest report")
mcp.anti_evasion_report.param_i: Derived scratch list: one path per line `<path> — <note>` (absolute or relative to cwd, globs allowed). List only scratch / intermediate artifacts you generated yourself that still exist now and await the user's decision (scratchpad scripts, .bak, one-off logs, undo files); do not list ones already deleted or pure explanations (default: delete when done). ⛔ Never list real deliverables: code / docs / atoms / indexes / CHANGELOG that were changed but not committed belong to the unsynced items of (a)(b)/(g), not scratch - such paths are rejected with a warning. The Python side parses this into the per-session leftover ledger, and those that still exist (by exists()) are listed for keep/delete. "none" if nothing. Required
mcp.anti_evasion_report.param_j_evidence: Persistent evidence path: where this turn's verification receipts persist, one absolute path per line. If this session ran a sentinel verification (Bash / PowerShell output `<NAME>_CHECK PASS|FAIL|DONE`), fill "none" or leave it blank: the system automatically fills in the absolute path of this session's receipt ledger (the ledger is in the data root, no need to find it); fill this only to attach other verification output / report files, and what you fill is used; the Stop reconciliation gate checks exists() and blocks if it does not exist. "none" if there are no receipts. Required
mcp.anti_evasion_report.param_k_followup: Follow-ups: things not finished and to be chased later, one per line `[<part>] <what to chase>` or `<part> | <what to chase>` (stored in the closing report; no follow-up ledger is written, no defect list is written, nothing is listed at session start). Write "none" if there are none; ⛔ an empty string is not accepted (Stop blocks). Required
mcp.anti_evasion_report.param_principles: Required, give [] if none was touched: wherever this time touched the user's long-term principles, design yardsticks or system direction, one item per place.
How you traded off this time, and why
Which principle / direction was touched, in plain language (the original wording may be quoted)
Optional: technical details; kept in a collapsed section
mcp.anti_evasion_report.param_report: Optional: a sentence or two as the opening (top of the report card) - who is doing what, who this message is for, whether the user needs to act. Put details in the three categories, do not repeat them here
mcp.atom_edit_meta.param_entry: Replacement Entry (entry-point code markers, e.g. ["E04"]; optional). Replaces the whole Entry line and the index entry field; [] clears.
mcp.atom_feedback.description: Vote that an injected atom was helpful or misleading for the task you just did. Votes are appended to `memory/_votes/<user>.jsonl` (version-controlled, so teammates' votes accumulate) and immediately update this machine's usefulness α/β that drives [{tentative}]→[{observed}]→[{fixed}] promotion. Call it when a card clearly saved you from a mistake, or clearly sent you the wrong way; do not vote on cards you did not actually use.
mcp.atom_promote.description: Promote an atom's confidence level. Eligible only by usefulness: Wilson lower-bound ≥ promote_lb with n ≥ min_n for [{tentative}]→[{observed}], n ≥ fix_min_n for [{observed}]→[{fixed}]. Confirmations and ReadHits are not promotion gates. Use execute=false for dry-run. When promoting to [{fixed}], pass merge_to_preferences=true to append knowledge into preferences.md and archive the source atom (global scope only).
mcp.atom_promote.param_merge_to_preferen: On [{observed}]→[{fixed}] promotion, auto-merge knowledge into preferences.md and archive this atom. global scope only. Default false.
mcp.atom_retire.description: Retire a useless / wrong atom nobody cites: clears its _atom_index.json entry, vector index and MEMORY.md directory line together, and moves the file to _distant/<yyyy_mm>/ (restorable: memory-audit --restore). All guards run before any change (single source in py): [{fixed}] is refused (use atom_write supersedes to replace it); core-protected names are refused (also refused if the protection list fails to load); atoms referenced by another atom's Related/Supersedes are refused (the scan includes the personal layer); a missing atom is an explicit error, not a success. If any index / vector / move step fails -> returns an error listing the completed and uncompleted steps. The last line of the result is the receipt (op=retire, old_path, new_path, index_ok); in knowledge_harvest_report, a retired item takes its old_path. This tool writes no state (one-writer: the receipt is booked by the Python PostToolUse).
mcp.atom_retire.param_dry_run: Run only guards and location, change nothing; returns the planned move path
mcp.atom_retire.param_reason: Required: why it is retired (written to audit / merge history)
mcp.atom_retire.param_scope: Layer the atom is in: global=~/.claude/memory/ (including Failures/); local=~/.claude/_AIDocs/_atoms/; shared/personal/role=project layer (needs project_cwd); org=organization layer (the shared of the config org_memory root, no project_cwd needed)
mcp.atom_retire.param_user: Owner for scope=personal (defaults to the current OS user)
mcp.atom_source.description: Look up where an atom came from: the Source pointer plus the Quote original words; if the transcript still exists, returns one message before and after that uuid verbatim (state=live), otherwise returns the Quote (quote_only), and if neither exists returns the origin and "original conversation past retention" (unrecoverable). Read-only, writes no state, leaves no receipt.
mcp.atom_source.param_cwd: Project root, used to locate project-layer atoms; defaults to the server process cwd
mcp.atom_source.param_format: Reply format: table (default) or json (raw JSON string)
mcp.atom_tools.blocked_exit:
Atom NOT written to shared/. Way out of pending review: /memoryatoms:conflict pending to view -> approve/reject
(backend: tools/conflict-review.py --list / --action approve|reject --target <name> --project-cwd <root>)
mcp.atom_tools.conflict_criteria: Criteria: the two describe the same thing in the same scope (same project, same tool, same setting key) and cannot both hold; different scopes that each hold, or one supplementing the other, are not conflicts.
mcp.atom_tools.conflict_ignored: [conflict-detector] conflict declaration ignored (no candidate over the threshold)
mcp.atom_tools.conflict_pending_cands: Atoms to declare on (top {count} by vector this time, independent of the local model's label; resend with the knowledge section unchanged and the list stays the same):
mcp.atom_tools.conflict_pending_head: Conflict declaration needed (nothing written this time): the similarity threshold and the local model's label only decide whether to ask (rule CONFLICT_DECLARED_BY_AI); whether it is a conflict is your call.
mcp.atom_tools.conflict_resend: Resend with conflict=[{"of": "<atom name>", "verdict": "conflict"|"not_conflict", "why": "<one-sentence reason>"}], one entry per atom above (extra entries not on the list are ignored, not an error): not_conflict -> written to shared as usual; conflict -> goes to the pending-review report and is not written to shared. Both are recorded.
mcp.atom_tools.conflict_type: conflict must be an array of {"of": "<candidate atom name>", "verdict": "conflict"|"not_conflict", "why": "<one-sentence reason>"}
mcp.atom_tools.dedupe_type: dedupe must be an object {"verdict": "same"|"supersedes"|"different", "of": "<candidate atom name>", "why": "<one-sentence reason>"}
mcp.atom_tools.idx_not_found: - Index entry {name} not found in _atom_index.json (nothing to remove)
mcp.atom_tools.idx_remove_failed: - ⚠ Index removal failed ({error}) — please clear the {name} entry in _atom_index.json by hand
mcp.atom_tools.merge_hint: 💡 Suggestion: {name} has reached the highest confidence level; if this knowledge is essentially a "personal preference / operating convention", call again with merge_to_preferences=true to merge its knowledge into preferences.md and archive this atom.
mcp.atom_tools.merge_skipped: [merge_to_preferences] skipped: only the global scope is supported.
mcp.atom_tools.move_prior_issues: ⚠ The index has {count} issue(s) that existed before this move (not caused by it; fix: shorten the trigger with atom_edit_meta or run tools/sync-atom-index.py --fix):
mcp.atom_tools.move_scope_synced: - File header `- Scope:` synced to the index scope
mcp.atom_tools.org_not_joined: {tool}: scope=org but this machine has not joined the organization memory (org_memory); join with: {cmd} --join [<local path>]
mcp.atom_tools.pending_exists: A same-name draft is already pending review: {path} — handle it with /memoryatoms:conflict pending first, or write under a different title
mcp.atom_tools.project_not_initialized: scope={scope} needs a project memory layer, but {cwd} has none yet (nothing was written). Option 1: initialize it (this creates .claude/memory in that project and nothing else), then call atom_write again: {cmd} . Option 2: call atom_write again with scope=global to write now; the card is then visible across all your projects.
mcp.atom_tools.readhits_line: ReadHits: {count} (exposure only, not part of promotion)
mcp.atom_tools.realm_hold: [atom_write] {rule}: {slug} is bound to Entry {entry} -> kept in core (the lexicon would have judged {would})
mcp.atom_tools.scope_reason_type: scope_reason must be a string (one sentence: why this passage is cross-project)
mcp.atom_write.param_conflict: Conflict declaration (scope=shared create). Send only when resubmitting after atom_write replied "conflict declaration pending (nothing written this time)" and listed the cards to declare on (the top vector hits this time): one entry per listed card; extra entries not on the list are skipped, not an error. Judge whether two cards are about the same thing in the same scope AND cannot both hold; different scopes that each hold, or one card supplementing the other, are not conflicts. not_conflict = write as normal; conflict = goes to a pending-review report, not written to shared. of = card name copied verbatim, why = one sentence. Both are recorded.
mcp.atom_write.param_dedupe: Dedup declaration (create). Send only when resubmitting after the write gate replied "declaration needed" (the new content resembles existing cards, candidates listed): state how the new content relates to one of the candidates. same = the same item, the knowledge is merged into that card (goes through append; triggers/actions are not merged); supersedes = replaces it, write the new card and mark that one with Supersedes (old card kept, no longer injected); different = distinct, write the new card as usual. of = candidate card name copied verbatim, or any other existing card in the layers searched for this dedup check (the reply's searched layers; same name in different layers is written <layer>:<card name>); why = one sentence of reasoning (blank, placeholder or punctuation-only is rejected). When nothing similar was hit, the declaration is followed as given: the of of same/supersedes must be an existing card in those layers; different writes as usual with a note.
mcp.atom_write.param_domain: Category path under the layer root: '<Lv1>[/<Lv2>]'. REQUIRED for mode=create when scope=global (non-local realm), for feedback-* titles (Lv1 = failure topic -> memory/Failures/<topic>/), and for scope=shared (-> shared/<Lv1>/). Lv1 is a CLOSED list (memory/_meta/taxonomy.json), given here as EN slugs: vcs | workflow | thinking | verify | dotnet | windows | text | design | conduct | cc-memory; slugs/aliases are accepted and snapped to the canonical category name (e.g. 'vcs/git' -> the vcs category, sub-folder Git). Lv2 is free (created on demand). Unknown Lv1 -> rejected unless allow_new_category=true. Ignored for append/replace (existing atom located via index). For realm=local this is instead the hierarchical local domain (e.g. 'MemDev' or 'OS/Windows/WSL'; roots World|Tools|MemDev; empty/invalid -> 'Else').
mcp.atom_write.param_dry_run: Preview without writing. create: runs the full gate chain (domain/category snap, [{tentative}] rule, write-gate dedup, build+validate, budget) and reports the landing path/category - no file, no index, no conflict-detector side effects. append/replace: locates the existing atom and reports what would change. Default false.
mcp.atom_write.param_entry: Entry-point code markers (e.g. ["E04", "E08"]). Rendered as `- Entry:`. A create with entry is not auto-routed to the local realm (ENTRY_BOUND_STAYS_CORE); with scope=global give a core domain. replace: omit=keep, []=clear; ignored on append.
mcp.atom_write.param_kind_hint: Optional. Declares the card's kind: pointer / complement / ledger (current-state ledger) / hub (reading guide) / plain. The py side still judges for itself (hub = kind_hint=hub, or the title contains 導讀 ("guide"), or all five sections are present; ledger = dates and numbers check out); a hint cannot let a card with missing sections through.
mcp.atom_write.param_knowledge: Knowledge lines (normally prefixed with [{fixed}]/[{observed}]/[{tentative}]). A single element starting with | (markdown table) or ``` (code fence) is emitted verbatim as a block, no bullet - pass tables/code as their own element.
mcp.atom_write.param_not_sensitive: Send only when resubmitting after the write gate said "may be personal verification or private information": one sentence explaining this is ordinary technical knowledge, not personal sensitive information (blank or punctuation-only is rejected; kept in the audit). If it really is sensitive, use secret=true instead. This field does not let through content containing real password or token values.
mcp.atom_write.param_provenance: Optional source of this knowledge: file path / URL / commit / session id. Rendered as `- Source:`. replace/append: omit=keep, ""=clear, non-empty=replace the whole Source line (append: include the old source in the value if it should stay).
mcp.atom_write.param_quote: The user's original words that triggered this card, single line, at most 200 characters; usually filled automatically by PostToolUse, callers need not supply it. Rendered as `- Quote:` (after Source). replace/append: omit=keep, ""=clear, non-empty=replace.
mcp.atom_write.param_scope: V4 scope. shared=project-wide, role=role-shared (requires `role`), personal=per-user (requires `user` or defaults to current). global=cross-project. org=organization layer (sugar: shared under workflow/config.json org_memory root; project_cwd ignored). project (legacy)=transparently mapped to shared. Defaults to shared. REALM GATE: when called from a project working dir, scope=global is REJECTED (all modes, skip_gate cannot bypass) if title/triggers/knowledge/actions mention any project-specific name (the project's top-level folder names, CLAUDE.md / Workspace_Map member names, repo-paths {codes}, absolute paths under the project root, or the literal phrases 此專案 / 本專案 / 這個專案 / 這專案 ("this project")) - use scope=shared + project_cwd instead; feedback-* titles then land in <project>/.claude/memory/failures/<domain>/.
mcp.atom_write.param_scope_reason: Scope reason (scope=global/org). Send only when the realm gate blocked solely because of literal wording such as "this project": one sentence on why this passage is cross-project (e.g. it is talking about the phrase itself). With it the write proceeds and is recorded; project-specific names and project paths still block, this field does not let them through.
mcp.atom_write.param_secret: Required for personal privacy-sensitive information (passwords, tokens, private keys, credentials, personal data, any verification or private content not meant to be public). true = stored under ~/.claude/memory/personal/<user>/secret/: not version-controlled, not sent to the vector index, visible only to the owner, trigger words still inject; scope is switched to personal automatically, other fields are filled as usual. Never write the value itself into the card, only where it is kept.
mcp.atom_write.param_secret_reason: Send only when resubmitting after a secret=true rejection: the write gate said "no sensitive wording matched" or "only some lines are sensitive, split the card", and you judge the whole card really must not be public -> one sentence saying which line and what information (kept in the audit). When sensitive and non-sensitive content are mixed, split into two cards instead of forcing this field.
mcp.atom_write.param_skip_gate: Skip the write-gate QUALITY/DEDUP check only (for [{fixed}] or explicit user request). Does NOT skip realm/scope checks: the project-name realm gate for scope=global and the category/domain gate always run.
mcp.atom_write.param_status: Optional one-line current status (e.g. 'closed 2026-07-29'). Shown alongside cold/one-line injections so the pointer carries minimal state. Current-state ONLY - no version history / change narrative.
mcp.atom_write.param_supersedes: Names of the old atoms this one replaces (create/replace). On replace: omitted = keep the existing Supersedes; [] = clear; non-empty = replace. Superseded atoms are no longer injected but the files are kept. The py side rejects: self-reference, cycles along the existing chain, targets that are core-protected names, targets that do not exist. Ignored on append.
mcp.boot_record.write_failed: [boot-record] cannot write the boot record (the hook cannot tell whether to block the reload advice, so it lets it pass): {error}
mcp.extension_dirs.old_registry: [Guardian:Migrate] extension {name}: rename {old} to {new} (the old name still loads)
mcp.funnel.resolution_approve: 2. If incoming has independent value -> approve (moves the draft to `shared/`)
mcp.funnel.resolution_edit: 1. Edit the existing atom or the incoming one — to resolve the factual conflict
mcp.funnel.resolution_reject: 3. If incoming is wrong -> reject (deletes only this report; the existing atom is untouched)
mcp.harvest.items_array: knowledge_harvest_report: items must be an array (give items=[] even when nothing was worth writing this session)
mcp.harvest.need_path: {tag}: action={action} requires path (the absolute path returned in the atom_write/atom_retire receipt)
mcp.harvest.rejected_tail: Fix and call again (for action other than skip, path must be the absolute path from the receipt; skip must carry a reason).
mcp.harvest.skip_reason: {tag}: action=skip requires reason (one sentence on why nothing is written)
mcp.instructions.intro: Atom memory: this server manages the team's knowledge cards - past decisions, pitfalls already hit, organization tools, project conventions. Your client has no hook that injects memory on every turn, so look things up and write them yourself.
mcp.instructions.search: Search: when an answer involves past decisions, pitfalls, organization tools or project conventions, or the user says things like "check memory" or "is it in the organization memory", call memory_search first (query = the question as asked; cwd = the current project root, which decides whose project cards are visible). To find out where a card came from, use atom_source.
mcp.instructions.where: Where cards live: global ~/.claude/memory/<category>/; project layer <project>/.claude/memory/; the org layer is in the attached organization memory repo. Indexes: ~/.claude/memory/MEMORY.md (category overview), _INDEX.md in each category folder, machine index ~/.claude/memory/_atom_index.json. Cards are Markdown and can be read directly; writes always go through atom_write.
mcp.instructions.write: Write: when the user says "remember this" or "save to the org layer", or you reach a conclusion worth keeping, use only atom_write (it validates the format, dedupes and updates the index); never edit card .md files directly. Scope: cross-project knowledge = global; this project's rules = shared (pass project_cwd); about this person only = personal; whole organization = org. New global/shared cards (mode=create) must carry domain. Passwords, tokens and personal data take secret=true; never write the value itself into the card.
mcp.knowledge_harvest_report.description: Stage-completion knowledge-harvest report: called when the Stop gate (KnowledgeHarvest) requires it on declaring completion. Order: first finish writing this session's knowledge worth keeping with atom_write (create/append/replace, supersedes), retire useless atoms with atom_retire, then call this tool to list the result of each inventoried item. Scan six sources: (1) user corrections / rejections / restatements (2) mechanisms / pitfalls that took >=2 retries or a lookup to understand (3) external facts (with date) (4) tradeoffs / contracts / preferences I made (5) existing atoms proven wrong or needing additions (6) atoms this session showed to be useless and uncited. Criterion: write only what "cannot be read from code/docs and will be looked up again or repeated"; one-off facts are not written (action=skip with a reason leaves a trace). action≠skip requires atom and path, where path must be the absolute path from the last-line receipt of the atom_write/atom_retire result (for retired, the pre-retirement path); items=[] means nothing this session was worth writing (the call is still required). When the closing self-check is due, put this into harvest_items of anti_evasion_report and submit once; no separate call to this tool is needed. This tool only returns a chip and writes no state (one-writer: item-by-item reconciliation of items against this session's receipts, and state/ledger, belong exclusively to the Python PostToolUse; if it does not reconcile, Harvest-Pending blocks once and asks for a fix).
mcp.knowledge_harvest_report.param_actio: Action already taken (completed before calling this tool); skip=judged not worth writing
mcp.knowledge_harvest_report.param_candi: Optional. This is really a cross-project rule, landed in shared only because the realm gate blocked it
mcp.knowledge_harvest_report.param_items: Inventory list; give [] if nothing this session was worth writing.
mcp.knowledge_harvest_report.param_path: Absolute path from the receipt (required when action≠skip; for retired, give old_path)
mcp.knowledge_harvest_report.param_reaso: Required when action=skip: one sentence on why it is not written
mcp.knowledge_harvest_report.param_route: Optional. Extraction route: part_doc=has a part -> that part's defect list plus a one-line pointer card (part required); global=cross-project after stripping project details; org=whole organization; local=memory system only; shared=project; candidate_global=landed in shared first after the realm gate refused, marked as a global candidate. The summary of global / candidate_global must not carry a project name (run atom_io_cli action=scrub first)
mcp.knowledge_harvest_report.param_sourc: Knowledge source: correction=user correction; mechanism=mechanism/pitfall; external_fact=externally found fact; decision=tradeoff/contract/preference; atom_fix=fix to an existing atom; atom_retire=retirement
mcp.knowledge_harvest_report.param_summa: One sentence on what this knowledge is
mcp.memory_search.description: One-sentence lookup of atom memory (read-only). Uses the same retrieval pipeline as hook injection: candidate pool (global + this project's shared + the user's own role/personal, scope visibility already narrowed) -> trigger / BM25 / vector -> RRF fusion ranking. Returns a stable schema_version=1 structure: results[{name, path, rel_path, scope, source, score, excerpt, author, audience, tags, status, provenance}] and warnings (same-name cross-layer shadowing, vector path disabled, etc.); provenance = the raw value of the atom's `- Source:` line (empty string means none). format=table (default, human-readable) | json (for programs / other AIs). Writes no state, leaves no receipt.
mcp.memory_search.param_cwd: Which project directory to search from (decides the project-layer candidate pool); defaults to the server process cwd
mcp.memory_search.param_format: Reply format: table (default) or json (raw JSON string)
mcp.memory_search.param_query: The question or keywords to look up (required)
